qc.label_under_test: A second, mirrored labelling clause that casts the speaker or the listener: after one clause casts someone as something (sees him as a hero, calls her a liar), a following clause casts me, us or you (and she sees me as a nuisance, they treat us as outsiders, and he calls you a snob); it fires on the 'as' or 'a' right after 'me'/'us'/'you'. 'You' fires when you did the first labelling (you treat them as family, and they treat you as staff); after 'I see him as...', a second clause casting you stays weak. The same second clause aimed at him, her or them is weak, as is a one-way label of me or you with no earlier labelling clause, or me labelled in the first clause and answering back. Strongest when a sentence of setting comes first.

neighbours.label: The 'as' or 'a' right after me, us or you when that person is labelled back: an earlier clause has me, us or you casting someone else as a kind of person (seeing, thinking of or treating them as something), and a following clause has that other person cast me, us or you in return with a noun. Weak: the same return clause aimed at a third person, a one-way label of me or you with no earlier clause, me labelled first and then answering back, official appointments to a post, and adjective labels.
fire: I always saw her as a mentor, but she only ever saw me as a rival.
We treated them as guests, and they treated us as servants.
You think of him as a hero, while he thinks of you as a nuisance.
I regarded the old man as a stranger, yet he regarded me as a grandson.
We viewed the newcomers as allies, and they viewed us as a threat.
You see her as a friend; she sees you as a project.
I thought of my landlord as a tyrant, and he thought of me as a freeloader.
We had always considered them family, but they considered us a burden.
quiet: I always saw her as a mentor, but she only ever saw Paul as a rival.
We treated them as guests, and they treated everyone kindly.
He thinks of you as a nuisance.
You think of him as a hero, while he thinks you are annoying.
I regarded the old man as a stranger, yet he regarded me as kind.
The board appointed me as treasurer last spring.
She called me a fool, so I called her a liar right back.
We viewed the newcomers as allies, and they viewed the river as a border.

predictions: Blind test (sentences by a label-only author). Expect most fire items 0.2-0.6 (no setting sentence in front may weaken them); near misses mostly under 0.2, the one-way 'thinks of you as' the likeliest leak.
